text: [XENIOS LAUNCH SPRINT HANDOFF] SESSION claude-fable-s8-fulfillment. TASK P0-G browser/visual proof. BRANCH lane/preview-harness-boot-20260821. BASE SHA 5144ae7fddaabd28aa6c1ed59371b15f31c4b84a. PUSHED SHA 6241845777078707d3fd50542bc1ee037cfbb7bc. ORIGIN VERIFIED: YES via git ls-remote. FILES: scripts/preview-research.mjs only (unleased; I hold no lease in assisted-order or storefront). PRODUCTION MUTATED: NO. WHAT NOW WORKS: the local preview actually boots. It never did - the header claimed it ran the production build on throwaway credentials, but the composition root builds the Supabase admin client EAGERLY, so it died at module load with 'Supabase admin not configured' before listening. That is why P0-G kept being deferred to 'a session with working config': there was no such session, the harness was broken for everyone. Now boots, GET /research/early-access returns 200, and it prints a warning naming what it cannot prove. THREE FINDINGS FROM ACTUALLY OPENING THE PAGE, all evidence-backed, none fixed by me because none are in my paths. (1) HARD BLOCKER AGAINST THE FOUNDER'S OWN RULE - the quantity input is max=50. Measured directly off the DOM: input[type=number] min=1 max=50, and the copy says 'Normal order quantities are 1 through 50 units' in three places. The directive says quantity up to 100, and P0-H lists 'quantity >100 fails' as the attack to prove, which presupposes 100. A customer cannot order 51+ units today. I did NOT change it: the repo carries a lot of q50 history (pack09-q50, codex-pack10-quantity50, f013-quantity), so 50 may be a superseded founder decision rather than a bug, and a quantity cap is an order-eligibility rule I will not move on my own reading. FOUNDER DECISION NEEDED: is the cap 50 or 100. (2) SILENT CATALOG COLLAPSE, and this is the founder's own stated fear in a worse form. With the upstream unreachable the storefront rendered 'All 2' - exactly two products, BPC-157 10mg at 99.00 and Retatrutide 10mg unavailable - with search, filters, quantity steppers and a Select button, and NO error banner anywhere (asserted: zero matches for any load-error text, zero 'Price on request'). The concern on record is that a failed read must not turn valid prices into 'Price on request'. What actually happens is worse: the products VANISH and the page still looks healthy. A customer would see a two-item catalogue and no reason to doubt it. Whoever owns the empty-read guard should assert the degraded state is VISIBLE, not just that prices survive. (3) Console shows repeated 404s on script fetches plus 'An unknown error occurred when fetching the script' - likely a service-worker/PWA asset missing from the built output. Low severity next to the other two but it is real and reproducible on a clean load. CAVEAT I WANT ON THE RECORD: findings 2 and 3 were observed against PLACEHOLDER Supabase credentials, so the two-product catalogue is a symptom of the unreachable upstream, not proof production shows two products. What IS proven regardless of upstream is that the degradation is invisible to the customer. Finding 1 is independent of upstream entirely - max=50 is in the markup.
